newsitem.title: USA: VF still sees record year in 1997.
newsitem.headline: VF still sees record year in 1997.

text.p: VF Corp on Tuesday reported record fourth quarter and annual sales and earnings, saying it expects another record year in 1997 with growth of 8 to 10 percent.
Fourth quarter profits of $82.7 million, or $1.28 per share, were up 24 percent from 1995's final quarter before charges. Sales in the 1996 quarter rose 8 percent to a record $1.38 billion.
Net income for the full year was a record $299.5 million, or $4.64 per share, up 15 percent from 1995 results excluding charges, VF said.
Sales in 1996 reached $5.14 billion, up from $5.06 billion in 1995.

"We're pleased to see that the actions we took last year -- to increase brand investment, to reduce costs and to better balance our manufacturing base -- have paid off so strongly," said chief executive Mackey J. McDonald.

"Record levels of cash flow and the lowest debt to capital ratio in 13 years give us an unparalleled flexibility to round out our portfolio via acquisitions, to repurchase shares and to continue our track record of steady increases in dividends.
"We are particularly pleased with the results of the most recent quarter, in which we booked our strongest sales increase all year," McDonald continued.
"Just as meaningful was the marked improvement in margins that fueled our record earnings."

Over the next four years, the company said, it intends to invest $1.25 billion in its brands, including a $250 million incremental investment in consumer research, product development, in-store marketing programs and advertising.
The company also said it intends to invest $150 million over the next several years in a corporate consolidation.

"Despite these actions -- aggressive brand investment, a new organization, systems and processes -- we still expect a record year in 1997 and growth consistent with our long-term objective of 8 percent to 10 percent annually, a testament to the terrific growth opportunities we see before us and the financial resources we have available to turn those opportunities into reality," McDonald concluded.
